title: Mixed Event — Nocturne Interlude — Episode3 Missing Pieces

meta.Event Outline: Toya has decided to create street music as a member of Vivid BAD SQUAD. But something happens to make him wonder if classical music still has some hold on him, leading to some self-doubt...

rows.Line: The next day
Weekend Garage

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Hello...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Hey, Toya. You're practicing here today, right? I saved a table for you guys, so feel free to use it.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Thank you very much.
I'll have... Coffee, please.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: You got it.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: (I've watched that video over and over and my voice is definitely the most rigid in the group...)

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: (What can I do to change that...?)

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line:
Hey, Toya. Sorry I'm late.
The soccer club got their grubby hands on me.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: It's okay...

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line:
What's with the doom and gloom?
Something bothering you again?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Something like that...
I've realized there's a major problem with my singing.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: To be honest, I'm not sure what I can do about it. Can I ask you for your opinion as well? If you don't mind... Hm?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: What's wrong? Why do you look so surprised.

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: I wasn't expecting you to just spill the beans like that.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: What do you mean...?

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: Think about it. You usually clam up when you have a problem.

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: And then sink deeper and deeper into self-doubt as you try to solve it by yourself. At least, that's what happened the last time we fought...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Now that you mention it...

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: But I guess this means you've sort of fixed that habit.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Looks like it.
It must be because of you, Akito.

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: Hmph. I'll take that as a compliment.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line:
Here's your coffee.
Same for you, Akito?

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: Sure, sounds good. Thanks.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Thank you, Ken.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: I used the best beans for this one. The aroma alone can brighten up just about anybody's day. Even yours, Toya.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: I don't know what's troubling you, but there's no need to beat yourself up about it.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Oh...

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: Ken... You noticed?

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line:
Just a feeling.
Comes with age, you know?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I'm sorry for making you worry...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line:
It's all a part of life.
So, did something happen?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Well, actually...

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: Classical music is making your singing too rigid, huh...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I grew up in the world of classical music after all.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: It's like how classically trained pianists usually can't play swing music well after switching to jazz.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Their minds are so set in their classical background that playing jazzy grooves is just beyond them. So maybe...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: You think that might be happening with you as well?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: There's something different about the way I sing compared to Akito. It's like I can't... Sing freely, maybe?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: That's probably why my style seems so rigid, while my songs sound stale.

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: I don't think so...

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: I wouldn't team up with someone who could only stick to cookie-cutter patterns.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line:
He's right.
I agree with him.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
No, wait...
It has to be true if Akito believes it.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Haha. Your partner has a lot of faith in you...!

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Still... I don't know why, but I just feel like I lack that freedom of expression.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: As if I'm still trapped in a sort of classical frame of mind.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Hmm... We think you sound perfectly fine, but if you're convinced there's something wrong with the way you sing...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Then isn't it obvious what the problem is?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Huh?

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: There's nothing wrong with the way you sing. Something other than classical music is bothering you, right?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Something else...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Looks like you have an idea.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes. But it's something I believe I've already settled...

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: Is this about your dad...?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Yes... Just the other day, he kept telling me to return to classical music and we ended up arguing over it.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: But I'm determined to continue chasing my dream with you.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Which is why I told my father that I'll never go back to classical music and I'm only going to pursue street music.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: He didn't seem convinced, but there's nothing I can do about that since we have such different values.

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: In my opinion, the matter should already be settled...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Hmm...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: But maybe it's not quite as settled as you think, Toya?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Huh?

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: From the way you talk about him, your father must've been a major presence in your life up to this point.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Maybe you're feeling guilty about following a path he disapproves of?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: That's...

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: That being said, it's not like you can just snap your fingers and make your father understand.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: You might as well prepare for the worst and confront him head-on if it's going to bother you like this.

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line:
Sorry I'm late!
Hall monitor duties went overtime today.

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: I'm sorry for being late too!

rows.Speaker: Akito
rows.Line: It's fine. We were just having a chat with Ken. Give us a holler once you're ready to start warming up, okay?

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line:
Wait, Toya? Are you okay?
You don't look too good...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: Don't worry, I'm fine...

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line:
Thank you for the advice, Ken.
I'll try to see if there's something I can do.

rows.Speaker: An's Father
rows.Line: Sure, but don't overdo it, okay?

rows.Speaker: Toya
rows.Line: I won't...

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line:
Oh, about our talk the other day...
My dad said he'd come watch us perform!

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: He'll decide whether a live house is dangerous or not after seeing one for himself!

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: Really?! That's great!

rows.Speaker: An
rows.Line: But you know, he might faint from shock after seeing how awesome you are?

rows.Speaker: Kohane
rows.Line: Hehe. That would be a bit embarrassing...
